title: Software
description: Types for building and shipping software.

types.title: Application
types.description: A software application the work uses or targets, such as Rhino or Revit.

types.title: Feature
types.description: A capability of a product. Built means merged but not yet in a release.

order.description: Position on the roadmap among its siblings. Lower comes first.

tokens_estimated.description: How many tokens an agent expects this to take in all: input and output, not counting cached re-reads. It stands only while none of the tasks that are part of it has an estimate: after that the feature is the sum of its tasks.

tokens_used.description: Tokens spent on it directly, measured from the sessions that worked on it. What its tasks used is added when it is shown.

types.title: Proof
types.description: Something a user would ask before trusting the software, such as how we know the sun is correct. The title is the question. It is answered on a build when every test of it passed there: that is worked out from the results, not stored.

types.title: Test
types.description: One check that helps answer a proof question. A draft is a test that is wanted and not yet written. What it found is kept per build, as test results.

compares.description: What is compared with what, in one line a user can read: the position of the sun against the NOAA calculator in six cities.

tolerance.description: How close it must be to pass, e.g. within 0.01 degrees.

environment.description: Where it runs and draws its picture: outside any host, in Rhino, in Revit.

types.title: Test result
types.description: What one test found on one build. There is one for each test on each build; a later run on the same build replaces it.

build.description: The version or commit the test ran on.

picture.description: Where the picture the test drew is: a path in the repository it ran in, under its .proof folder, which git ignores. The file itself is sent to Archipelago (picture_put) only when the result is shown in public.

types.title: Environment
types.description: Somewhere software runs: a machine, a VM, staging, production.

types.title: Handoff
types.description: Where a working session left things for the next one.

relations.title: lives in
relations.description: The repository that holds the work.

relations.title: uses
relations.description: An application the work depends on or targets.

relations.title: helps answer
relations.description: The test is part of how we know. A proof question is answered on a build when every test that helps answer it passed there.

trees.title: Roadmap
trees.description: A project's features in the order they are to be built, the work under each, and where work is happening now.
